questions.question: What is the difference between a plugin and an application on the ServiceNow AI Platform?

options.text: A plugin adds features to installed applications and extends platform functionality; an application is a standalone piece of code that implements a collection of features
A plugin is always purchased from the ServiceNow Store; an application is always activated by ServiceNow personnel
A plugin is a custom table; an application is a custom field
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable

explanation.correct: A plugin adds features to installed applications and extends functionality on the platform. An application is a standalone piece of code that implements a collection of features, and can be installed from the ServiceNow Store or built yourself. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_ServiceNowPlugins.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Plugins cannot be purchased through the ServiceNow Store, and many applications are installed by admins.
Plugins and applications are software components, not tables or fields.
The documentation explicitly describes plugins and applications as separate components.

source.excerpt: A plugin adds features to installed applications and extends functionality on the ServiceNow AI Platform. … An application is a standalone piece of code that implements a collection of features

questions.question: An administrator activated a plugin in a sub-production instance and now wants to remove it. What does the documentation say?

options.text: After a plugin is activated it cannot be deactivated; functionality can be hidden, for example by restricting access with roles and ACLs
Plugins can be deactivated at any time from Application Manager
Plugins are automatically deactivated after 30 days if unused
Deactivation requires reverting the last update set

explanation.correct: After a plugin is activated, you cannot disable or deactivate it. If needed, you can hide or disable the functionality by restricting access with roles and ACLs, and some plugins support rollback contexts. This is why plugins should be tested in a non-production instance first. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_ServiceNowPlugins.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no general deactivate option for activated plugins.
Plugins do not expire or deactivate automatically.
Plugin activation is not captured in an update set that can be reverted.

source.excerpt: After a plugin is activated, you can't disable or deactivate it.

questions.question: A plugin that an administrator needs does not appear in Application Manager. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Request activation of the plugin by ServiceNow personnel through the Now Support Service Catalog
Import the plugin as an update set from another customer
Create the plugin record manually in the sys_plugins table
Clone production over the development instance

explanation.correct: If a plugin does not appear in Application Manager you cannot activate it yourself. Request activation by ServiceNow personnel, either through the Now Support Service Catalog or via Request Plugin in Application Manager. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_RequestAPlugin.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Plugins are provided by ServiceNow and are not distributed as customer update sets.
Plugins cannot be created by manually inserting records.
Cloning does not make a missing plugin available for activation.

source.excerpt: If a plugin does not appear in the Application Manager, you cannot activate it yourself. Request activation of the plugin by ServiceNow personnel.

questions.question: What happens when an administrator activates a plugin that depends on other plugins?

options.text: The system lists the dependencies and, if the administrator continues, automatically activates the required plugins
Activation fails until each dependency is activated manually
The dependencies are ignored and only the selected plugin is activated
ServiceNow support must approve each dependency first

explanation.correct: When you activate a plugin with dependent plugins, the system notifies you of the dependencies before it completes the activation. If you continue, the system automatically activates all the plugins required. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/c_ServiceNowPlugins.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The system handles required dependencies automatically when you continue.
Required dependencies are activated too, not ignored.
No separate support approval is required for dependencies of a plugin you can activate.

source.excerpt: If you opt to continue with activation, the system automatically activates all the plugins required.

questions.question: Which statement about obtaining plugins is correct?

options.text: Plugins can't be purchased through the ServiceNow Store
Plugins are only available by writing custom code
Every plugin must be bought separately in the ServiceNow Store
Plugins can only be activated on personal developer instances

explanation.correct: Plugins are provided by ServiceNow. Some are pre-activated and others can be activated by you or by ServiceNow personnel. New plugins become available during upgrades in line with your licensing, and plugins can't be purchased through the ServiceNow Store. Applications are what you try, buy, or get from the Store. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/plugins-apps-products-integrations.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Plugins are provided by ServiceNow, not written by customers.
Applications, not plugins, are obtained through the Store.
Plugins are activated on customer instances, not only PDIs.

source.excerpt: Plugins can’t be purchased through the ServiceNow Store.

questions.question: According to ServiceNow, what is an integration?

options.text: A type of app that connects your instance to systems outside the ServiceNow ecosystem
A collection of apps that work together as a product
A plugin that is always pre-activated
A report that combines data from two tables

explanation.correct: An integration is a type of app that connects your instance to various systems outside the ServiceNow ecosystem. Products are collections of apps that work together. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/plugins-apps-products-integrations.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: That describes a product, not an integration.
Integrations are apps, not pre-activated plugins.
Reports are analytics artifacts, not integrations.

source.excerpt: An integration is a type of app that connects your instance to various systems outside the ServiceNow ecosystem

questions.question: Your company purchased an application from the ServiceNow Store. What must happen before it is active on the instance?

options.text: An administrator installs it from Application Manager on the instance
It activates automatically on all instances at purchase
A developer must import its source code with an import set
ServiceNow activates it during the next family upgrade

explanation.correct: Applications purchased from the ServiceNow Store are added to Application Manager automatically, but you must install the application from Application Manager to activate it in an instance. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_InstallApplications.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Purchase makes the app available in Application Manager; it still needs to be installed.
Import sets load data, not applications.
Store apps are installed by the customer from Application Manager, not activated during an upgrade.

source.excerpt: You must install the application from the Application Manager to activate it in an instance.

questions.question: While installing a Store application on a development instance, an administrator sees a Load demo data check box. What does selecting it do?

options.text: Installs sample records that describe application features for common use cases
Copies production data into the development instance
Installs the application in read-only mode
Skips installation of the application's dependencies

explanation.correct: Demo data are sample records that describe application features for common use cases. ServiceNow recommends loading demo data when you first install the application on a development or test instance. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_InstallApplications.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Demo data is sample data shipped with the app, not production data.
The check box has nothing to do with read-only mode.
Dependencies are listed and installed with the application regardless.

source.excerpt: Demo data are the sample records that describe application features for common use cases.

questions.question: A developer wants to try a plugin on their personal developer instance (PDI) that is not active by default. What does the documentation say?

options.text: They can activate it without requesting or purchasing it, although some plugins aren't available on PDIs
They must purchase a subscription first
Plugins cannot be activated on PDIs
They must open a case with ServiceNow for every plugin

explanation.correct: If a plugin isn't active by default on a PDI, you can activate it without requesting or purchasing it, from the All Applications page or the Developer Site. Some plugins aren't available for activation on PDIs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/activate-plugin-pdi.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: No purchase is needed to activate a plugin on a PDI.
PDIs support plugin activation, with some exceptions.
A support case is not required for plugins that can be activated on a PDI.

documentation.section: Activate a plugin on a personal developer instance

source.excerpt: If a plugin isn't active by default on a PDI, you can activate the plugin without requesting or purchasing it.

questions.question: In the classic environment, which navigation path lists the applications and plugins available to install or activate?

options.text: All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All
All > System Definition > Tables
All > System Update Sets > Retrieved Update Sets
All > Self-Service > My Requests

explanation.correct: To install an application or activate a plugin, navigate to All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All, find the item, and install or activate it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_InstallApplications.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition > Tables lists database tables.
Retrieved Update Sets lists update sets brought in from other instances.
My Requests shows a user's catalog requests.

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All.

questions.question: An administrator needs to add a system property that is not visible in the instance by default. Where are system properties stored?

options.text: In the System Property [sys_properties] table, reachable by typing sys_properties.list in the navigation filter
In the User Preference [sys_user_preference] table
In the Dictionary [sys_dictionary] table
In an update set

explanation.correct: Some system properties aren't visible by default and must be added to the System Property [sys_properties] table. Enter sys_properties.list in the navigation filter, check that the property does not already exist, then select New. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_AddAPropertyUsingSysPropsList.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: User preferences store per-user settings, not system properties.
The dictionary defines fields, not system properties.
Update sets capture configuration changes; they are not where properties are stored.

source.excerpt: must be added to the System Property [sys_properties] table

questions.question: Why does ServiceNow advise against storing configuration that changes more than once or twice a month in a system property?

options.text: Every change flushes the cache to keep cluster nodes in sync, which has a high performance cost
System properties can hold only 10 characters
System properties are deleted during every upgrade
Only the maint user can change system properties

explanation.correct: System properties store configuration that rarely or never changes. Each time a property is changed or added, the system flushes the cache to keep all nodes in the cluster in sync, which has a very high performance cost for one to 10 minutes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_AddAPropertyUsingSysPropsList.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The documented issue is cache flushing, not value length.
System properties persist across upgrades.
Admins and users with the defined write roles can change properties.

source.excerpt: Each time you change or add a system property, the system flushes the cache to keep all nodes in the cluster in sync.

questions.question: What does selecting the Private option on a system property do?

options.text: It excludes the property from being imported via update sets, so values in one instance don't overwrite another
It hides the property from all administrators
It encrypts the value in the database
It makes the property apply only to the user who created it

explanation.correct: Setting a property to private excludes it from being imported via update sets. This keeps settings in one instance, such as development, from overwriting values in another instance, such as production. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/t_AddAPropertyUsingSysPropsList.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Read and write roles, not the Private flag, control who can see or change a property.
The Private flag is not an encryption setting.
System properties are instance-wide, not per user.

source.excerpt: Set this property to true to exclude this property from being imported via update sets.

questions.question: An instance still uses Core UI (Next Experience is not enabled). Which module lets an administrator set the company logo, header colors, and system defaults such as the default time zone?

options.text: System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16
Theme Builder
System Definition > Dictionary
Service Portal > Branding Editor

explanation.correct: The Basic Configuration UI16 module, at All > System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16, lets administrators brand a Core UI instance with a logo and colors and set defaults such as the system time zone and date format. For Next Experience theming, use Theme Builder instead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/t_ConfigureLogoColorsSysDfltsUI16.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Theme Builder is for Next Experience themes; this module applies to instances without Next Experience.
The Dictionary defines fields and tables, not branding.
The Service Portal Branding Editor styles a portal, not the Core UI.

documentation.section: Configure logo, colors, and system defaults for Core UI

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16. … This information is only applicable for instances that do not have Next Experience enabled.

questions.question: Which tool reflects your company's brand in Next Experience by letting you create, edit, and publish themes without writing code?

options.text: Theme Builder
Form Designer
Schema Map
Transform Map

explanation.correct: Theme Builder lets you create and manage Next Experience themes for web and mobile experiences without writing code, including colors, logos and typography. It is included as a core plugin with Next Experience and is available by default. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/configuring-next-experience-with-theme-builder.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Form Designer configures form layouts.
Schema Map shows table relationships.
Transform maps map import set fields to target tables.

documentation.section: Configuring Next Experience with Theme Builder

source.excerpt: Create and manage Next Experience themes for your mobile and web experiences without needing to write code. … Theme Builder is included as a core plugin with the Next Experience and is available by default.

questions.question: In Theme Builder, what is the difference between a variant and an alternate color palette?

options.text: A variant is an alternate version of a theme, usually for accessibility (such as a Dark variant); an alternate color palette is a cosmetic color change
A variant changes the logo only; an alternate color palette changes form layouts
A variant applies only to Core UI; an alternate color palette applies only to mobile
They are the same record type with the same purpose

explanation.correct: A variant is an alternate version of an existing theme, usually designed for accessibility, which users can select in preferences. An example is the Dark variant of the default theme. An alternate color palette is a cosmetic modification to a theme's colors. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/difference-themes-variants.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Variants are alternate theme versions, and palettes change colors, not form layouts.
Dark variants don't apply to Core UI, so this is reversed.
Both are UX style records categorized as Variant, but the documentation says they serve different purposes.

documentation.section: Core styles, colors, variants, and alternate color palettes

source.excerpt: A variant is an alternate version of an existing theme, usually designed for accessibility … An alternate color palette is a modification that you can make to a theme's colors and is designed for cosmetic purposes.

questions.question: What is the Core UI?

options.text: The interface you use if Next Experience is inactive; it predates the Next Experience UI
A mobile app for agents
The Service Portal home page
The UI Builder design canvas

explanation.correct: The Core UI, previously called UI16, predates the Next Experience UI. It is the interface you use if Next Experience is inactive. Dark variants from Theme Builder don't apply to it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/difference-themes-variants.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Core UI is the classic browser interface, not a mobile app.
Service Portal is a separate self-service interface.
UI Builder is a tool for building workspace and portal experiences.

documentation.section: Core styles, colors, variants, and alternate color palettes

source.excerpt: The Core UI is the interface you use if Next Experience is inactive.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: In the Core UI, which component provides links to all applications and modules and is also called the left-navigation bar?

options.text: Application navigator
Banner frame
Content frame
Activity stream

explanation.correct: The Core UI is made up of the banner frame across the top, the application navigator (left-navigation bar) with links to all applications and modules, and the content frame that displays lists, forms, dashboards, and wizards. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/c_UI16.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The banner frame runs across the top with the logo, user menu, search, and settings.
The content frame displays lists, forms, and dashboards.
The activity stream shows a record's history and journal entries, not navigation.

source.excerpt: Also called the left-navigation bar. Provides links to all applications and modules.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: Which ServiceNow interface is designed mainly for agents, giving a single view of work with analysis and AI-based recommendations?

options.text: Workspace UI
Service Portal
Content Management System
Core UI banner frame

explanation.correct: The Workspace UI offers improved agent efficiency, faster resolution, and monitoring for major incidents, with data in a single view complete with analysis and AI-based recommendations. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/configure-uis-and-portals.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Portal is the self-service experience for end users.
CMS is for building websites and integrated apps.
The banner frame is only the header of the Core UI.

source.excerpt: All this data is provided from a single view, complete with analysis and AI-based recommendations.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: Which interface is ServiceNow's option for designing a self-service experience for end users, customizable from basic configuration to in-depth scripts?

options.text: Service Portal
Workspace UI
Form Designer
Studio

explanation.correct: Service Portal is used to design the self-service experience. It can be customized with anything from basic configuration to in-depth scripts and web apps. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/configure-uis-and-portals.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Workspace UI is aimed at agents rather than end-user self-service.
Form Designer configures form layouts.
Studio is an application development environment.

source.excerpt: Design the optimal self-service experience with Service Portal.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: In Next Experience, how can you tell from the Globe icon that you are working in an application scope other than Global?

options.text: A red circle icon is displayed
The header turns grey
The All menu is hidden
A banner appears on every form

explanation.correct: The Globe lets you select the application scope and update set. Any application scope other than Global displays a red circle icon. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The header color does not change with the application scope.
The All menu remains available.
No form banner is documented for scope changes.

source.excerpt: Any application scope other than Global displays a red circle icon

questions.question: A new customer starts on the Australia release. What do they need to do to get the Next Experience UI?

options.text: Nothing; Next Experience is enabled automatically
Activate the Next Experience plugin from the ServiceNow Store
Request Next Experience from ServiceNow support
Set glide.ui.polaris.experience to false

explanation.correct: New customers on the Australia release have Next Experience enabled automatically and don't need to change the UI. Existing customers without UI customizations get Next Experience when they upgrade. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/next-experience-adoption-paths.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: No Store plugin is needed for new customers.
No request to support is needed.
Setting that property to false disables Next Experience.

source.excerpt: If you're a new customer, you automatically have Next Experience enabled and you don't need to modify the UI to get the newest user interface.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: Which system property value disables Next Experience on an instance?

options.text: glide.ui.polaris.experience set to false
glide.ui.next.experience set to off
glide.ui16.enabled set to true
glide.ui.polaris.theme set to classic

explanation.correct: Setting the glide.ui.polaris.experience property to false disables Next Experience. UI16 must be installed before Next Experience can be activated. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/next-experience-adoption-paths.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is not the documented property name.
This is not the documented property.
This is not the documented property.

source.excerpt: Set the value of the glide.ui.polaris.experience property to false to disable Next Experience.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: Which UI must be installed before you can activate Next Experience?

options.text: UI16
UI15
Service Portal
Classic Workspace

explanation.correct: You must have UI16 installed before activating Next Experience. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-user-interface/next-experience-adoption-paths.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI15 is an older interface and isn't the documented prerequisite.
Service Portal is a portal framework, not the prerequisite.
Classic Workspace isn't the prerequisite.

source.excerpt: You must have UI16 installed before activating the Next Experience.

subtopics: Common user interfaces in the Platform

questions.question: Which statement about applications in the global scope is correct?

options.text: They can be uploaded to the application repository but not to the ServiceNow Store
They always get a unique namespace identifier
They are fully protected from other global applications
Only ServiceNow can create them

explanation.correct: Global scope applications don't add a unique namespace identifier, so they can have naming conflicts. They bypass scope protections, can be uploaded to the application repository but not to the ServiceNow Store, and can be created by developers with the sn_g_app_creator.app_creator role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/application-development/c_GlobalScope.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Global applications don't append a namespace identifier.
Global applications bypass scope protections.
Developers with sn_g_app_creator.app_creator can create global applications.

source.excerpt: Applications in the global scope are eligible for upload to the application repository, but not to the ServiceNow Store.

questions.question: An administrator wants to hide the impersonation button in the banner for users. Where is this configured?

options.text: All > System Properties > UI Properties, using 'Enable impersonation button in the banner line'
User Administration > Roles
System Security > Access Control (ACL)
Service Catalog > Maintain Items

explanation.correct: Before users can impersonate someone, an administrator must make the feature visible. Go to System Properties > UI Properties and use the 'Enable impersonation button in the banner line' check boxes. Admins can still impersonate through the impersonate_dialog UI page. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/user-administration/manage-the-visibility-of-the-impersonation-feature.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Roles don't control banner button visibility.
ACLs aren't where this UI property is set.
Catalog maintenance is unrelated.

documentation.section: Manage the visibility of the impersonation feature

source.excerpt: Select a check box under Enable impersonation button in the banner line to display or conceal the button.

questions.question: What is the difference between scoped apps and global apps?

options.text: Scoped apps are free; global apps require licensing
Scoped apps restrict access to their files and data by default; global apps bypass scope protections
Global apps are more secure than scoped apps
There is no difference

explanation.correct: Application scoping protects applications by identifying and restricting access to their files and data. By default, custom applications have a private scope with a namespace identifier, and other applications can't change their tables and logic without permission. Global applications are all in the same scope, so they bypass scope protections. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The difference is about access scope, not licensing costs.
Scoped apps are more secure because they have restricted access.
There is a significant difference in system access and security.

source.excerpt: Application scoping protects applications by identifying and restricting access to application files and data.
